Sample.evidence_source: Eighteen men were approached and 15 men agreed to participate in the full study and met the study inclusion criteria.

Country.evidence_source: recruitment efforts focused on outpatient settings within the University of Toronto psychiatric network

Population.evidence_source: Mental health service providers were asked to refer patients to the study if they met the following criteria: male, 18 years of age or more, a history of suicidal behavior

Type.evidence_source: A trained interviewer conducted face-to-face, audiotaped interviews that were transcribed verbatim.

Area.evidence_source: The analyses focused on identifying the similarities and differences between participants in terms of their interactions with a variety of health service providers. As well, we analyzed specific practices and episodes. Practices are important units of analyses because they are categories of talk and/or action (Lofland & Lofland, 1995) that are repeated across a range of situations. Episodes refer to positive and negative experiences that are "remarkable and dramatic to participants" (Lofland & Lofland, 1995). Analysis of episodes provided an opportunity to understand how these unusual experiences may have influenced later interactions. ... The purpose of this analytic process was to provide a rich understanding of the issues identified and to understand, where possible, the determinants of these issues.
